headline: Habagat Keeps Western Luzon Under Heavy-Rain and Flood Warnings
seoTitle: Habagat Keeps Western Luzon Under Heavy-Rain Warnings | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA says Habagat will continue bringing heavy rain to western and central Luzon on August 30, with red rainfall warnings issued over Zambales, Bataan and parts of nearby provinces.
deck: PAGASA warns of continued monsoon rains and serious flooding risk in parts of western and central Luzon as saturated communities face another day of heavy rainfall.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Southwest Monsoon or Habagat continued to bring heavy rain across western and central Luzon on Sunday, August 30, with PAGASA maintaining flood and landslide warnings in several provinces.

In its 4 a.m. forecast, PAGASA said monsoon rains would affect Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac and Pampanga. Metro Manila and several nearby provinces were forecast to receive occasional rains.

sections.heading: Rainfall warnings
paragraphs: At 5 a.m., PAGASA placed Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga and parts of Tarlac and Bulacan under a red rainfall warning, indicating serious flooding in flood-prone areas. The warning areas were adjusted again in the 8 a.m. advisory as rain bands moved.

PAGASA's heavy-rainfall outlook also indicated that 100 to 200 millimeters of rain could fall over parts of western and northern Luzon through Sunday and into Monday, with impacts potentially worsened in mountainous areas and locations already saturated by previous rain.

sections.heading: Low-pressure area
paragraphs: As of 3 a.m., PAGASA also monitored a low-pressure area about 1,340 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon. The system was not the primary source of Sunday's rain, but atmospheric conditions around the region can continue to influence the monsoon flow.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Western Luzon has endured repeated heavy-rain episodes in recent days. Even where rainfall temporarily eases, swollen waterways, saturated soil and residual floodwater can keep communities at risk.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should follow PAGASA rainfall warnings and local disaster advisories because warning levels and affected areas can change quickly. People in flood-prone or landslide-prone communities should comply with evacuation instructions when issued.
